title: Conduct Continuous Cleaning and Sanitising of the Abattoir

lessons.title: Cleaning during production
lessons.html:
Continuous cleaning

In an abattoir, cleaning does not only happen at the end of the day. It goes on all the time while the line is running. This is called continuous cleaning. It stops dirt, blood and fat from building up and keeps meat safe.

Your cleaning tasks during the shift

  • Knives and hands: sterilise knives in the hot water steriliser and wash hands at the hand-wash station after every carcass and whenever they touch the hide, gut contents or the floor.
  • Aprons and mesh gloves: rinse them at the apron wash when they become dirty.
  • Floors: scrape up fat, meat scraps and hair with a squeegee and shovel into the right bin. Keep the floor free of slippery fat.
  • Platforms and equipment: rinse blood and fat off platforms, saws and stands when your supervisor tells you, without splashing carcasses.
  • Drains: keep drain screens in place and clear the solids from them.
  • Bins: empty bins before they overflow and take them to the correct waste area.

Do not splash

When you hose near carcasses, keep the water low and point it away from meat. Splashing from the floor carries germs onto the carcass. Never hose a floor where carcasses or offal are hanging just above it.

Check the hygiene equipment

At the start of the shift and during the day, check:

  • sterilisers are full and hot (at the set temperature, commonly at least 82 °C),
  • hand-wash stations have soap, water and paper towels,
  • footbaths at entrances are filled with fresh sanitiser.

Report any that do not work. Do not use a cold steriliser.

Safety

Hot water and steam burn. Keep hands away from the hot steriliser water. Wear non-slip boots and walk carefully on wet floors.

lessons.title: End-of-day cleaning and sanitising
lessons.html:
The cleaning steps

At the end of production, the whole plant is cleaned and sanitised. Follow the cleaning schedule and these steps in order:

  1. Prepare: remove all meat, offal and carcasses from the area. Switch off and lock out machines. Cover electrical boxes if instructed.
  2. Dry clean: scrape and shovel all solid waste into bins. Do not hose solids into the drains.
  3. Pre-rinse: rinse surfaces with warm water, from top to bottom.
  4. Detergent: apply the detergent at the correct strength and scrub or let it soak for the time on the label. Detergent removes fat and protein.
  5. Rinse: rinse well with clean water to remove all detergent and loosened dirt.
  6. Sanitise: apply the approved sanitiser at the right strength. Sanitiser kills the germs that are left.
  7. Final rinse if the label says so, then let surfaces drain and dry.
  8. Check: look for remaining fat, blood or residues. Clean again if needed. The supervisor or quality controller inspects before production starts.

What to clean

Work from top to bottom and from clean areas to dirty areas: rails, walls, platforms, equipment, tables, trays, then the floor and finally the drains.

Using chemicals safely

  • Read the label and the safety data sheet.
  • Wear gloves, goggles, an apron and boots.
  • Measure the chemical; never guess.
  • Never mix chemicals. Some mixtures (like chlorine with acid) give off poisonous gas.
  • Store chemicals in their labelled containers in the chemical store, away from meat.
  • If chemical gets in your eyes, rinse with clean running water for a long time and get help.

Record the cleaning

Sign the cleaning checklist: area, date, time and your name. These records show inspectors that the plant is clean.

Key points

  • Clean continuously during the shift: knives, hands, aprons, floors and bins.
  • Do not splash water from the floor onto carcasses.
  • End-of-day steps: dry clean, rinse, detergent, rinse, sanitise, check.
  • Work top to bottom and clean to dirty.
  • Never mix chemicals and always wear PPE.

options.text: Cleaning that goes on all the time while the line runs

quiz.question: What is the first step in end-of-day cleaning, after preparing the area?

options.text: Dry clean: scrape solids into bins

quiz.question: In which order should you clean an area?

options.text: Top to bottom, clean areas to dirty areas

quiz.question: What should you do if a steriliser is cold?

options.text: Report it and do not use it

quiz.question: Mixing chlorine with acid can give off a poisonous gas.
Hosing the floor under hanging carcasses is good practice.
Which hygiene equipment should be checked during the shift? (select all that apply)

options.text: Hand-wash stations have soap and paper towels
Knife sterilisers are full and hot
